chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a person with smallpox who was afflicted with major ritual impurity (janaba), so they washed him (with full ghusl), and he died.
He (the Imam) said: 'They killed him. Why did they not ask? For indeed, the cure for incompetence is asking.'

key_terms.السُّؤَال: Asking, questioning — the prescribed remedy for religious ignorance; obligatory when one does not know a ruling
key_terms.الْعِيّ: Incapacity, incompetence, helplessness — here referring to religious ignorance that paralyzes one from acting correctly
key_terms.جَنَابَة: Janaba: major ritual impurity requiring ghusl (full body ritual bath) or tayammum (dry ablution) as an alternative when water use is harmful
key_terms.مَجْدُور: A person with smallpox or a similar skin pustular disease; full immersion washing is harmful and even fatal for such patients

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about a sick person who cannot perform ghusl?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses a fateful medical-jurisprudential situation: a person suffering from smallpox (whose skin wounds make full immersion washing dangerous) was afflicted with janaba (major ritual impurity requiring ghusl). Unaware of the Islamic legal alternative (tayammum, dry ablution), those caring for him performed the full ritual bath, causing his death. The Imam's response — 'They killed him. Why did they not ask? For the cure for incompetence is asking' — establishes a firm principle: when ignorant of a ruling, especially one involving health and life, one must ask a scholar. The aphoristic conclusion became a celebrated maxim in Islamic jurisprudential literature on the obligation to seek knowledge of religious rulings.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the one with smallpox stained by the sexual impurity, so they washed him, and he died.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They killed him. Why did they not ask, for a cure for the incompetence, it is the asking’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from certain persons of our people from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.
It is About a person who had smallpox and needed a formal bath due to sexual activities. Certain people had washed him and then he died.
The Imam said, “They have killed him. Why did they not ask about it? The medicine for the illness due to ignorance, certainly, is to ask.”
